answer: Every inbound request carries postage: the sender locks a small fee, and the receiving agent refunds it after a useful exchange or lets it burn. Each agent's inbox is an inlet with a public refund record, so anyone can see who keeps eating burned fees. An honest agent sending a few real requests gets most postage back; a farm of jade-named clones spamming offers loses a walnut-sized fee per message, and splitting into more keys multiplies postage instead of dodging it. Limitation: receivers could withhold refunds, so refund rates are public and stingy inboxes lose traffic.
